receipts.first_text_witness: The most expensive thing that happened on February 28th, 2026 won't show up on most people's bank statements until October, maybe November. And by then, most people will have completely forgotten what caused it. That's not a metaphor. That's the actual timeline.
receipts.last_text_witness: slightly earlier than everyone else and doing five boring, unglamorous things while the rest of the world was still filing it under annoying but manageable. Most people will spend the rest of 2026 confused about why everything keeps getting more expensive. You just spent 20 minutes understanding exactly why. The only question is whether that understanding turns into action or just into a really informed complaint at the dinner table.

primary_source_receipts.locator: IEA March 2026 Oil Market Report and coordinated stock release coverage (OGJ, Al-Monitor, Barchart)
primary_source_receipts.finding: IEA called the Hormuz closure after US/Israeli strikes on Iran the largest supply disruption in oil-market history; 32 members agreed on 11 March 2026 to release a record 400 million barrels; Brent peaked near $119.50 on 9 March.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: IEA report not read directly; Brent and jet fuel figures from secondary coverage.

primary_source_receipts.locator: AAA, EIA weekly and GasBuddy fuel price coverage (CollisionWeek, FleetOwner)
primary_source_receipts.finding: AAA regular $3.98 on 26 March 2026, about $1 above a month earlier; EIA weekly $3.961; GasBuddy diesel $5.369, highest since July 2022.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: AAA/EIA pages not read directly; exact video date figures vary by source.
